name: app2-two-node
note: Eisenberg & Noe non-uniqueness counter-example, Appendix 2 ([lu-archive] K4). Two nodes owe 1 to each other, p̄=[1,1]. With e=(0,0) no value enters: Φ(p)=(Πᵀp)∧1 and p=[1,1] as well as p=[0,0] are fixed points ⇒ p⁺=[1,1] ≠ p⁻=[0,0], NOT unique (negative control). With e=(0,01, 0) the system is regular ⇒ p⁺=p⁻=[1,1], unique (Thm 2: e>0 sufficient; here a single component >0 suffices because each node has a path to value).
